lines.text: We left Greyhollow with sixty fighters, twelve wagons, and one very large dog. Bram stayed behind with the rest, to keep the village safe. I didn't like leaving him. He didn't like being left.
Bring them all back, my lord. Every one.
I intend to.
It took nine days to reach the muster field at Senn Ford. My father's banners covered the hillside. Three thousand men. Knights in steel, levies in leather, and lords everywhere you looked.
We arrived last. Everyone noticed.
Is that the Greyhollow levy? Farmers, with a dog?
I hear the zero has been selling lamps to merchants. Trade. How embarrassing.
And then my brother rode up on a white warhorse, in black and gold armour, looking exactly like a hero from a song.
Little brother! You came! And you brought farmers. How sweet.
Hello, Maric. Father summoned the levy. Here it is.
Keep them at the back, would you? Real soldiers will handle the fighting. Your people can dig latrines.
Can I shoot him? Just a little?
Not today.
That night I went looking for the quartermaster. I wanted to know how three thousand men were being fed.
The answer was: badly.
Grain for twelve days, my lord. Maybe ten. The barges from the south are late, and the roads are all mud.
Ten days of food. Corrow had two thousand men across the river, with supply lines running straight back to their own granaries. All they had to do was wait, and my father's army would starve.
Nobody else seemed to have noticed. They were too busy planning glorious charges.
Tobin. How many wagons did we bring?
Twelve, my lord. Eight of them full of turnips.
Turnips. Eight wagons of glasshouse turnips. Enough to feed this army for two more weeks.
I went to find my father.
He was alone in his tent, studying a map. He didn't look up when I came in.
You came.
You summoned me.
I summoned a name on a list. I didn't expect you to answer.
Father, the army has ten days of grain. I've brought two more weeks. And I have an idea about the river.
For the first time in my life, my father looked at me as if I might be worth listening to.
Sit down.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter eleven, coming soon.
